name: United World Colleges
deadline: Set by your national committee; 2027 entry routes are open
eligibility: Typically age 16–17 at entry; local criteria vary
funding: Need-based scholarships through national committees and eligible pathways; self-funded places also exist
summary: A two-year international education that brings students from different countries together to learn, live and act for peace and sustainability.
tagline: Live and learn with the world.
heroImageAlt: UWC students holding flags from different countries
about: UWC is a global movement of schools and colleges that uses education to bring young people across cultures, countries and backgrounds. Its two-year International Baccalaureate route combines demanding academics with service, outdoor learning, creativity and shared residential life. Students apply to the movement, often through a volunteer national committee, and may be placed at different UWC schools according to availability and selection.

The purpose is larger than a diploma. UWC asks students to listen to perspectives unlike their own and turn what they learn into action for peace and a sustainable future. Daily life is intentionally international: lessons, meals, shared rooms, activities and community work become places to practice cooperation.

Applicants should pay close attention to their route. National committees set local deadlines and assess students in context. More than 80% of students selected through national committees receive financial support based on need, while the Global Selection Programme is a full-fee route. The official application guide explains which route fits each applicant.

history.title: An idea shaped by cooperation
history.text: Educational pioneer Kurt Hahn was inspired by people who had recently been on opposite sides of war working together. He imagined a school where young people could build understanding across borders.

history.title: The first college opens
history.text: UWC Atlantic admitted its first students in Wales, starting the international education movement.

history.title: National committees take shape
history.text: Volunteer committees began selecting students locally and widening access to UWC places.

history.title: A global network
history.text: UWC reports 18 schools and colleges and more than 85,000 alumni from over 180 countries since 1962.

experiences.title: IB learning

experiences.title: A residential community

experiences.title: Service in action
experiences.text: Join community action and activities that connect learning to real needs beyond campus.

experiences.title: International exchange
experiences.text: Build friendships and perspectives through dialogue, collaboration and living together.

name: Future Leaders Exchange
location: Host communities across the United States
deadline: Country-specific selection round; verify with the official FLEX site
eligibility: High school students from participating Europe and Eurasia countries; national rules vary
funding: Merit-based scholarship funded by the U.S. Department of State
summary: Spend an academic year at a U.S. high school, live with a volunteer host family and become a cultural ambassador for your home country.
tagline: One school year. A new perspective on the world.
heroImageAlt: FLEX exchange students at the June 2019 end-of-year gathering
about: FLEX is a competitive exchange scholarship for high school students from participating countries in Europe and Eurasia. The U.S. Department of State funds the program. Selected students spend a school year in the United States, attend an American high school and live with a volunteer host family.

The exchange is built around mutual understanding. Students share their culture with American classmates and neighbors while learning how another community studies, celebrates, serves and solves problems. The host family, school and local organization form a support network throughout the year.

FLEX selection is demanding and country-specific. The U.S. Department of State describes a multi-stage public application process. Eligibility and deadlines change by country, so an applicant should use the official FLEX site for the current local round rather than relying on a universal deadline.

history.title: A new exchange vision
history.text: The U.S. FREEDOM Support Act created a framework for educational exchange with countries emerging after the Soviet Union's dissolution.

history.title: FLEX begins
history.text: The Future Leaders Exchange program launched to strengthen long-term ties and mutual understanding between the United States and Europe and Eurasia.

history.title: An enduring alumni network
history.text: The Department of State reports more than 32,000 FLEX alumni across 24 countries over the program's history.

experiences.title: Host family life
experiences.text: Become part of a U.S. household and learn the rhythms of daily life in a new community.

experiences.title: American high school
experiences.text: Take classes, meet classmates and explore clubs, sports or arts at a local school.

experiences.title: Community service
experiences.text: Volunteer, share your culture and contribute to the community hosting you.

experiences.title: Leadership and exchange
experiences.text: Build the confidence to represent your country and maintain connections through the alumni network.

applySteps: Check whether FLEX recruits in your country and read the local eligibility criteria.
Follow the official country application process and its current selection dates.
Prepare to explain your interests, adaptability, leadership and willingness to share your culture.

name: Lumiere Research Scholar Program
deadline: Cohort-based; confirm the current round on Lumiere's official site
duration: 12 weeks to one year, depending on track
eligibility: Currently enrolled high school students; track requirements may differ
summary: Work one-to-one with a PhD mentor to shape an original research question, investigate it and produce an independent paper.
about: Lumiere Education connects ambitious high school students with PhD mentors for independent research. Instead of entering an existing lab assignment, a student develops a question in a chosen field and works through a guided research process with one-to-one support.

The project moves from reading and research design to analysis, writing and a final paper. Topics can span science, technology, social sciences or the humanities. Longer tracks include additional support for students who want to pursue publication, while the core value is learning how to think and work like a researcher.

The program is delivered remotely, which makes mentorship possible for students without nearby university research access. It is tuition-based, with financial aid offered by Lumiere. Program length and costs vary by track, so families should check the current official program details before applying.

history.title: A research mentorship model begins
history.text: Lumiere says it was founded by Harvard and Oxford researchers to help high school students work one-to-one with PhD mentors.

history.title: A wider research community
history.text: Lumiere reports more than 7,200 students mentored since 2020 and student work published in more than 50 academic journals. These are Lumiere-wide figures, not Relay outcomes.

experiences.title: Find a question
experiences.text: Choose a topic worth investigating and narrow it into an achievable research project.

experiences.title: Meet a PhD mentor
experiences.text: Work individually with a researcher who guides reading, methods and critical thinking.

experiences.title: Write a paper
experiences.text: Turn findings into a coherent independent paper with an academic structure.

experiences.title: Explore publication
experiences.text: Longer tracks can add guidance for submitting work to a student or academic journal.

name: Yale Young Global Scholars
organizer: Yale University Office of International Affairs
deadline: Early Action: 15 Oct 2026; Regular Decision: 6 Jan 2027, 11:59 pm ET
eligibility: Current high school sophomores or juniors, age 16–18 by 18 Jul 2027; other criteria apply
funding: Need-based aid and selected scholarships, including possible full tuition coverage
summary: Live on Yale's campus for two weeks of lectures, small seminars and conversations with young people from around the world.
tagline: A global classroom on Yale's campus.
heroImageAlt: Students at Yale Young Global Scholars
about: Yale Young Global Scholars is a residential pre-college program run by Yale University's Office of International Affairs. Each summer, high school students from across the world spend two weeks on Yale's campus in an academic track centered on science and technology, politics and economics, or global challenges.

The days combine Yale faculty lectures with smaller seminars led by undergraduate and graduate instructors. Students test ideas with peers, collaborate on projects and experience the social side of university life in residential colleges. The program is designed to make global conversation a central part of academic learning.

Admission is competitive, and eligibility is specific to the 2027 cycle. Students must be current high school sophomores or juniors and meet age, graduation and English fluency requirements. Need-based financial aid is available to applicants from all countries; applicants should review the official deadlines and aid instructions before submitting.

history.title: Ivy Scholars begins
history.text: Yale faculty and administrators started a small pre-collegiate summer program to bring future leaders together across borders.

history.title: A global identity
history.text: The program was renamed Yale Young Global Scholars to reflect its international conversation and ambition.

history.title: Experiments beyond New Haven
history.text: YYGS offered sessions at Yale-NUS College in Singapore and Yale Center Beijing in China.

history.title: Back on campus
history.text: After three online summers during the pandemic, YYGS returned to in-person programming at Yale.

experiences.title: Faculty lectures
experiences.text: Hear Yale scholars introduce big questions and current ideas across your track.

experiences.title: Small seminars
experiences.text: Discuss evidence and arguments with undergraduate and graduate instructors and an international cohort.

experiences.title: Residential life
experiences.text: Live in Yale residential colleges, share meals and join community events with other scholars.

experiences.title: Capstone collaboration
experiences.text: Work with peers to synthesize learning into a project and present it at the end of the session.

applySteps: Check the 2027 age, grade, graduation and English requirements on Yale's eligibility page.
Choose an academic track and decide whether to apply by Early Action or Regular Decision.
Prepare your activities list, essays, school transcript, recommendation and financial aid materials if needed.
